narrative:
The model predicts a 30% chance that you will not pass your final year, which means there is a significant risk of failing. This prediction is based on several factors that have been shown to influence student performance.

One of the most important factors is your aspiration for higher education. While this is a positive goal, it appears that your current academic habits may not align with achieving it. The model indicates that students who are less engaged in their studies, particularly those who study for less than two hours a week, are more likely to struggle. In your case, this limited study time is a concern, especially when compared to the majority of students who dedicate more time to their studies.

Another significant factor is your history of past failures. Although you have not failed any classes yet, the model suggests that students with a clean record often have better outcomes. This means that while you have a good starting point, maintaining that momentum is crucial.

Lastly, your social activities, particularly how often you go out with friends, also play a role. Students who spend more time socializing may find it harder to focus on their studies, which could impact their grades.

To improve your chances of passing, consider increasing your study time and finding ways to balance your social life with your academic responsibilities. Engaging in extra support, whether through tutoring or study groups, could also be beneficial. Taking these steps can help you align your efforts with your aspirations for higher education.
